name: Dark Diva Blue
lede: Dark Diva Blue is a muted, greyed blue, ColorHub's library name for a darkened shade of [[diva-blue]], traced to Ridgway's 1912 color atlas.

sections.title: A darkened diva blue
sections.body:
The name follows ColorHub's modifier grammar, "dark" plus the parent color [[diva-blue]] [1]. The library dates the swatch to Ridgway's *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* of 1912, plate XXI, and again places it in the ISCC-NBS Dictionary of Color Names of 1955, in the block for strong purplish blue [1]. Ridgway's plates survive only as scans of an aged, printed chart, so the hex value is an approximation of the original ink, not a measurement of it [1].

The closest named neighbors on file are [[indigo-blue]] and [[sailor-blue]], both close enough to read as the same color at a glance [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a color within six units of this swatch, covering at least five percent of the canvas, in 48 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 per cent, as photographed [2]. It is rare before the twentieth century, then rises in the 1910s: 6 of the 520 paintings we hold from that decade, nearly six times the archive's rate [2]. The counts are small, and three of the 48 are by Edvard Munch [2]. These are computed color matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
